question: What is used in the preparation of calcium sulphate hemihydrate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gypsum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gypsum** (CaSO₄·2H₂O) is used in the preparation of **calcium sulphate hemihydrate** (CaSO₄·0.5H₂O).
 
• Calcium sulphate hemihydrate is commonly known as **Plaster of Paris**.
 
• The process involves **heating gypsum** to around 150°C to 180°C, which partially dehydrates it.
 
• Plaster of Paris is widely used in **construction, sculpture, and medical applications** for making casts and molds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gypsum**:

 
 
• It is a soft sulfate mineral composed of calcium sulfate dihydrate.
 
• Gypsum is naturally occurring and is mined from sedimentary deposits.
 
• It is used in various industries, including agriculture as a soil conditioner and in the production of cement.
 
 
 
• **Plaster of Paris**:
 
 
• It is a quick-setting gypsum plaster consisting of a fine white powder (calcium sulfate hemihydrate).
 
• When mixed with water, it rehydrates and sets quickly, making it useful for casting molds and medical bandages.
 
 
 
• **Dehydration Process**:
 
 
• The heating of gypsum to produce Plaster of Paris is a controlled process to ensure partial dehydration.
 
• Overheating can lead to complete dehydration, forming anhydrite (CaSO₄), which has different properties.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Plaster of Paris**:
 
 
• In construction, it is used for making decorative elements and false ceilings.
 
• In orthopedics, it is used for making casts for broken limbs.
 
• In art, it is used for making sculptures and other decorative items.
